title: The Birdcatcher and the Lark
summary: A birdcatcher was busily spreading fine horsehair nets across a stubble field and scattering sweet millet seeds upon the ground to entice woodland birds....
full_text:
A birdcatcher was busily spreading fine horsehair nets across a stubble field and scattering sweet millet seeds upon the ground to entice woodland birds.

A crest-lark perched upon a wild rose bush watched him from afar and asked curiously: "Good sir, what magnificent work are you engaged in with those ropes and pegs?"

The birdcatcher smiled warmly and replied: "I am laying the foundations of a grand, prosperous new city where all creatures may live in abundance and peace!"

With these words, the man retreated into the bushes.

The simple lark, captivated by the promise of a peaceful city and enticed by the scattered grain, fluttered down to feast. The moment his claws touched the seed, the snare snapped shut, tangling his delicate wings in the horsehair cords.

As the birdcatcher stepped forward to wring his neck, the lark wept in bitter despair: "Alas! If this is the kind of city you build, master builder, you will find very few citizens willing to inhabit it!"
moral: Beware the treacherous stranger who lays traps while pretending to build a city.
